preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is between 1 and 500 inclusive.
The number of edges m is between 0 and the maximum possible edges for n vertices.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct vertices within the valid range [1, n].
The list of edges contains exactly m unique pairs with no duplicates.

postconditions.description: The first line of output is either 'Yes' or 'No'.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == 'No' or (len(output_lines) == 2 and len(output_lines[1]) == n and all(c in 'abc' for c in output_lines[1]))
postconditions.description: If the answer is 'Yes', the second line contains a string of length n consisting only of 'a', 'b', and 'c'.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == 'No' or (all((s[u-1] == s[v-1]) or (abs(ord(s[u-1]) - ord(s[v-1])) == 1) for u, v in edges) and all((s[u-1] != s[v-1]) and (abs(ord(s[u-1]) - ord(s[v-1])) != 1) for u, v in non_edges))
postconditions.description: If the answer is 'Yes', the string s satisfies the graph condition: an edge exists between u and v if and only if s[u] and s[v] are equal or adjacent in the alphabet ('a'-'b' or 'b'-'c').

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == 'Yes' if exists_valid_string(n, edges) else output_lines[0] == 'No'
postconditions.description: The output 'Yes' is printed if and only if there exists at least one valid string s that generates the given graph G.
